name: Good surgical instrument kit
note: Reliable bronze and iron surgical blades, forceps, and spatulas are already the baseline wherever there is skilled metalworking.

name: Cataract couching
note: Displacement of opaque lens via a hollow needle, an ancient technique attested from Mesopotamia through Rome to India. The rev is patient fees.

name: Trepanation
note: Drilling into the skull to relieve pressure or expel evil spirits. Infection and death are common; emergency cases will still be paid for.

name: Amputation and prosthetics
note: Rapid limb removal to prevent gangrene. High mortality from shock and infection. Prosthetics of wood and leather follow for dignity and limited function.

name: Wound suturing
note: Linen thread with bronze needle, removing thread after 2-3 weeks. Works well for clean wounds.

name: Military field hospital (valetudinaria)
note: Permanent structure with wards, built adjoining barracks. The state mandates these for legions. Clean water, drainage, and isolation of contagion cut mortality by half.

name: Opium and mandrake tinctures
note: Poppy and mandrake extracts in oil, applied topically or given orally. Dosing is unpredictable; overdose causes death or stupor.

name: Herbal pharmacy (Dioscorides Materia medica)
note: Dioscorides' Materia medica describes 600+ plants. Effective for many uses: willow bark for pain, elderflower for fever. The physician's reference work.

name: Bone setting
note: Reduction and splinting of fractures. Success depends on immobility for weeks; infection is the main hazard.

name: Obstetric practice
note: Manual assistance, podalic version, ergot to hasten delivery. Maternal mortality is 1-2%; assistance often makes it worse.

name: Aqueducts and public latrines
note: Abundant clean water and sewage separation are already established wherever aqueduct and drainage engineering has matured. This infrastructure, once mature, is the foundation for any public health improvement.

name: Legal protection for physicians
note: Imperial edict: physicians who follow established methods are not liable for death. This requires establishing consensus on best practice.

name: Ligature over cautery for haemostasis
note: Tying off vessels with linen before cutting. Slower than cautery but less tissue damage and no scar contracture. Requires training to isolate arteries.

name: Asepsis, antisepsis, and steam sterilization
note: Asepsis: prevention of contamination. Antisepsis: chemical disinfection. Steam sterilization beats carbolic spray because it kills spores, not just surface germs.

name: Autoclave for steam sterilization
note: Sealed vessel with high-pressure steam at 120 C for 15 minutes sterilizes instruments. Requires precision engineering; leaks render it useless.

name: Surgical barrier masks and hand coverings
note: Boiled linen masks and disposable or freshly sterilised hand coverings reduce droplets and direct contamination only when combined with hand washing and sterile technique; cloth is not equivalent to impermeable rubber.

name: Handwashing protocol (Semmelweis)
note: Handwashing and instrument cleaning between autopsy and delivery. Maternal mortality dropped from 18% to 1% in Vienna 1847. The physician who discovered this was committed to an asylum.

name: Ether, chloroform, and nitrous oxide anaesthesia
note: Diethyl ether (first 1846) is explosive and irritates airways. Chloroform (1847) is smoother but causes cardiac arrhythmias in 1 per 3000. Nitrous oxide is safest but partial. Pain-free surgery is a miracle.

name: Cocaine for local anaesthesia (UNOBTAINABLE)
note: Cocaine is derived from coca, a New World plant. UNOBTAINABLE before oceanic trade. The substitute is opium solution injected locally, less effective and systemic.

name: Hypodermic syringe and hollow needle
note: Glass or silver barrel with accurately bored needle. Intravenous injection becomes possible. Contamination of the needle kills; strict asepsis required.

name: Blood groups and transfusion
note: ABO typing discovered 1900. Before this, transfusion killed 1 in 5 from agglutination. Citrate prevents clotting. Saves haemorrhage victims.

name: Saline and fluid resuscitation
note: Isotonic salt solution administered intravenously. Restores blood volume and prevents shock. Simpler and saves more lives than transfusion.

name: Stethoscope and percussion
note: A rolled tube of paper or wood detects heart and breath sounds. Tapping the chest reveals fluid or consolidation. Simple but requires training to interpret.

name: Clinical thermometer
note: Mercury in glass with fixed point at 37 C. Temperature tells severity of infection. Fever is sometimes the body fighting infection.

name: Sphygmomanometer (blood pressure cuff)
note: Cuff inflated by hand, releasing air while watching mercury and listening to pulse. Requires precision machining and a mercury barometer.

name: Ophthalmoscope
note: Mirror and lens to view the retina. Reveals aneurysms, cotton-wool spots, diabetic changes. Requires skilled assembly.

name: Endoscope
note: Tube with lens at the far end, mirror to reflect light. Inspection of bladder, urethra, rectum. Illumination by candlelight makes diagnosis difficult.

name: X-ray imaging
note: Cathode ray tube generating X-rays to expose plates. Reveals fractures and foreign bodies. HONEST WARNING: repeated exposure causes burns and cancer. Protection is inadequate.

name: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
note: Electrodes on chest and limbs, galvanometer recording heart's electrical activity. Detects arrhythmias and infarction. Requires stable power and shielded wiring.

name: Microscopy in pathology with histology
note: Aniline dyes from coal tar make cells visible for the first time. Methylene blue, carmine, safranin stain bacteria and tissue. Identifies cancer, tuberculosis, syphilis. Beautiful dependency on the chemical branch.

name: Bacterial culture and Gram staining
note: Petri's shallow agar dishes allow colonies to grow. Gram staining distinguishes by cell wall: crystal violet for gram-positive, red for gram-negative. Guides antibiotic choice.

name: Sterile technique
note: A complete ritual: sterile drapes, fields, gowns. No cross-contamination. Requires training and discipline. One careless move ruins everything.

name: Vaccination: variolation to attenuated vaccines
note: Variolation: pus from smallpox pustule (0.5-2% death). Cowpox: Jenner's insight, much safer. Pasteur: heat or chemical attenuation for rabies, anthrax, cholera. Toxoids (diphtheria, tetanus) are safest.

name: Antitoxin and serum therapy
note: Serum from horses immunized with toxin. Diphtheria antitoxin reduced mortality from 50% to 20%. Anaphylaxis kills 1 in 1000. Passive immunity is temporary.

name: Epidemiology, statistics, and vital registration
note: John Snow mapped cholera deaths (1854); they clustered around one well. Data beats theory. Vital registration (births, deaths, cause) is the denominator. Null hypothesis testing reveals truth.

name: Case control and randomised controlled trials
note: Case control: backward look at exposure. Fast and cheap. Randomised controlled trial: random assignment to treatment or placebo, prospective, blind. Eliminates bias but takes years.

name: Quarantine, clean water, and sewage
note: Isolation of sick (quarantine). Filtration removes suspended matter. Alum coagulant precipitates colloids. Chlorination kills pathogens. Sewage separation and S-bend traps prevent backflow.

name: Vector control and drainage for malaria
note: Malaria is endemic to many marshy lowlands of the ancient world (Rome's own marshes are the best-documented case). Drainage of standing water eliminates mosquito breeding. Laborious but works.

name: Nutrition, deficiency diseases, and vitamins
note: Scurvy (vitamin C), rickets (vitamin D), beriberi (thiamine), pellagra (niacin), goitre (iodine). Iodised salt eliminates endemic goitre. Vitamin concept emerges from analytical chemistry.

name: Insulin extraction and purification
note: Extract from porcine pancreas, crystallize, purify. Banting and Best 1921. Before insulin, diabetes is death. Now: life and productivity.

name: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid)
note: Acetylation of salicylic acid (from willow bark). Safer than salicylate because absorbed slowly. Reduces fever, pain, inflammation. Bayer trademark.

name: Sulfonamides (sulfanilamide)
note: First broad-spectrum antibiotic 1935, derived from aniline dyes. Inhibits bacterial folate synthesis. Saves millions from streptococcal and gram-negative infections.

name: Penicillin extraction and purification
note: Penicillium mold produces beta-lactam antibiotic. Deep-tank fermentation and chromatography extraction are industrial operations. HONEST: this is not bedroom chemistry.

name: Antiseptic obstetrics and incubator
note: Handwashing before delivery, clean gowns, sterile towels. Puerperal fever drops from 25% to 2%. Incubator for prematurity: warm box with temperature control increases survival from 10% to 40%.

name: Dentistry and high-speed drill
note: Electric motor driving high-speed burr removes decay and drills for filling. Eliminates hand-cranked slowness and pain.

name: Spectacles and refraction testing
note: Ground lenses with trial frame testing. Corrects myopia, hyperopia, astigmatism, presbyopia. One of medicine's easiest wins.

name: Hospital as an institution with records
note: Permanent structure with wards, admission records, diagnosis, treatment, outcome. Allows tracking disease patterns and training the next generation.

name: Nursing as a trained profession
note: Formal training programme for nurses. Florence Nightingale proved competent nursing cuts mortality by half. The profession becomes medicine's backbone.

name: Medical education and cadaver dissection
note: Formal curriculum: dissection of cadavers, demonstration, case study. Several ancient societies restrict human dissection on religious or legal grounds (Rome forbids it outright, so physicians there must apprentice illegally or learn abroad); check whether an equivalent restriction applies to your own society.

name: Forensic medicine and autopsy
note: Autopsy to establish cause of death. Time of death, toxicology, physical evidence. The state pays well for conviction support.
